findings.title: traceID field dropped from 'Plugin Request Completed' log line
findings.body: The old logRequest implementation explicitly computed `tracing.TraceIDFromContext(ctx, false)` and appended a "traceID" key/value to logParams whenever a trace ID was present. That code (and the `tracing` import) was removed in this PR and not replaced anywhere: the new `instrumentContext` helper in contextual_logger_middleware.go only adds `endpoint`, `pluginId`, `dsName`, `dsUID` and `uname`, never `traceID`. As a result, the "Plugin Request Completed" log entries emitted by LoggerMiddleware no longer contain the trace ID, making it harder to correlate plugin request logs with distributed traces unless pkg/infra/log's FromContext independently injects trace correlation (which is not evident from the diff). This looks like an unintentional regression rather than a deliberate removal.

findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext discards state, breaking assertions on logged calls
findings.body: TestLogger.FromContext(_ context.Context) Logger always returns a brand new `NewTestLogger()` instance instead of returning the receiver (or a logger that still records into the original fields). LoggerMiddleware now logs via `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)` (logger_middleware.go), so any test that supplies a `*TestLogger` to code under test and later inspects `InfoLogs`/`DebugLogs`/etc. on that original instance will always see zero calls, because the actual Info() call lands on a throwaway logger that is discarded immediately afterward. This silently defeats the purpose of the fake logger for any code path that calls FromContext before logging.

findings.title: No unit tests added for the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware
findings.body: This PR extracts the previously-embedded `instrumentContext` logic into a new standalone ContextualLoggerMiddleware (and exported constructor NewContextualLoggerMiddleware), but no test file (e.g. contextual_logger_middleware_test.go) was added to verify which fields are placed on the context, that QueryData/CallResource/CheckHealth/CollectMetrics are instrumented while SubscribeStream/PublishStream/RunStream intentionally are not, or that the middleware correctly feeds LoggerMiddleware downstream. Given this logic directly affects what shows up in production logs, lack of coverage is a real gap.

findings.title: Test function name not updated after Instrumentation -> Metrics rename
findings.body: The file was renamed from instrumentation_middleware_test.go to metrics_middleware_test.go and the internal constructor call was updated to `newMetricsMiddleware`, but the top-level test function is still named `TestInstrumentationMiddleware`. This leftover name contradicts the stated goal of the PR (renaming for clarity/consistency) and will confuse anyone searching for tests related to MetricsMiddleware.

findings.title: Missing documentation of required middleware ordering for context propagation
findings.body: The previous InstrumentationMiddleware had a doc comment explicitly stating it "should live at the top of the middleware stack" because it both instrumented metrics and enriched the context with a contextual logger. That constraint has now shifted to require ContextualLoggerMiddleware to sit immediately before LoggerMiddleware in CreateMiddlewares (so the enriched context created by ContextualLoggerMiddleware reaches LoggerMiddleware's `FromContext` call). No comment documents this ordering requirement in either contextual_logger_middleware.go or the CreateMiddlewares slice, so a future reorder of middlewares (e.g. moving NewLoggerMiddleware before NewContextualLoggerMiddleware) would silently drop contextual log fields (pluginId, endpoint, uname, dsName/dsUID) with no indication of why.

findings.title: Adding FromContext to the Logger interface is a breaking change for all implementers
findings.body: The exported `plugins/log.Logger` interface gained a new method `FromContext(ctx context.Context) Logger`. Any other implementation of this interface in the codebase (mocks, adapters, etc.) that isn't updated in this PR will fail to compile. Only `grafanaInfraLogWrapper` (logger.go) and `TestLogger` (fake.go) were updated here; it should be verified that no other implementers of plugins/log.Logger exist elsewhere in the repository (or in downstream consumers of this package) that would be broken by this interface extension.
